how_this_section_is_used: Nothing here is implemented on the strength of this page. Each suggestion carries two or three paths with their cost, risk and what they unlock. A reviewer records a choice in console/data/decisions.json; only then does the work start. Until a choice is recorded the status is 'awaiting review'.

rows.title: Fail the build when the results feed is behind the official schedule
rows.problem: The feed holds 1 of 14 Week-10 results. Nothing failed, so any number computed today silently describes last week.
rows.buys: Every published weekly number carries a trustworthy as-of date.
rows.risk: A stale feed will start failing builds that used to pass.

options.path: Hard gate
options.detail: Compare the last final in the feed with the last final on the official schedule page; fail the build on any gap.
options.risk: Builds fail on Mondays until the feed refreshes.

options.path: Warning plus timestamp
options.detail: Print the staleness in days on every page and let the build pass.
options.risk: A warning at the top of a page is easy to ignore.

rows.recommended: Hard gate

rows.title: Put a clock time and raw bytes on every injury read
rows.problem: Captures carry a date only, and we store rendered text rather than the page we read. Two reads cannot be ordered within a day, and a transcription cannot be audited.
rows.buys: The report becomes a series instead of a snapshot, which is the precondition for every injury feature the brief asks for.
rows.risk: Raw HTML is large; the repository will grow.

options.path: Commit raw bytes to the repository
options.detail: Keep it simple and auditable; accept repository growth.

options.path: Store outside the site and keep a hash here
options.detail: Satisfies the brief's durability requirement and keeps Pages small.

rows.recommended: Store outside the site and keep a hash here

rows.title: Schedule the Wednesday, Thursday and Friday injury capture
rows.problem: We hold three reads taken on a Saturday, Sunday and Monday. Practice trends inside a week are invisible.
rows.buys: Designation changes become observable, which is the only honest way to use the injury signal.
rows.risk: A scheduled job can fail silently; it needs an alert.

options.path: GitHub Actions cron
options.detail: Runs in this repository's existing Actions setup.
options.risk: Silent failure unless an alert is added.

options.path: Cron plus a freshness alarm
options.detail: The job and the check that it ran.

rows.recommended: Cron plus a freshness alarm

rows.title: Make the injury signal a change, not a level
rows.problem: Counting how many players are Out is a level. It carries no news, because the market already knows it.
rows.buys: A signal that can move a line instead of one that restates the table.
rows.cost: Blocked until S03 lands and four weeks of captures exist.
rows.risk: With too few reads the change is mostly noise.

options.path: Wait for four weeks of captures, then difference
options.detail: Correct, but nothing ships this season until November is out.

options.path: Use last season's archive to prototype the formulation now
options.detail: The historical feed has designations back to 2016, but only one read per week, so the change must be week-over-week.
options.risk: Week-over-week is a weaker proxy than within-week.

rows.recommended: Use last season's archive to prototype the formulation now

rows.title: Measure what each designation is worth before using it
rows.problem: 'Questionable' has no official percentage and we have never measured one.
rows.buys: A calibrated number instead of a borrowed one, and an interval that says how much to trust it.
rows.cost: Two days once the join is built.
rows.risk: The measured rate may be so wide that the feature is not worth having. That is a result, not a failure.

options.path: Join three seasons of designations to the official inactive lists
options.risk: Needs the inactive lists, which we hold for one week only.

options.path: Buy or scrape the inactive lists first, then measure

rows.recommended: Join three seasons of designations to the official inactive lists

rows.title: Fix the club-code mapping once
rows.problem: nfl.com prints AZ for Arizona and LA for the Rams; the repository stores both AZ/ARI and LA/LAR in different files.
rows.buys: Every cross-file join becomes safe.
rows.risk: Renaming breaks pages that read the old codes.

options.path: One alias table, enforced at build time
options.detail: A single mapping; the build fails on an unknown code.

options.path: Alias table plus a compatibility shim
options.detail: Safer for the pages that already exist.
options.risk: Two places to keep in step.

rows.recommended: One alias table, enforced at build time
rows.evidence: Captured this session from the official standings page

rows.title: Capture the reserve lists so 'not listed' stops meaning 'available'
rows.problem: A player absent from the injury report may be on injured reserve. The official reserve list is now captured for November 2026, and 15 of its 25 players are invisible in the weekly report — but only one month is captured and no join exists.
rows.buys: Every per-team injury count we publish stops under-counting.
rows.risk: The reserve list may not be published in a machine-readable form.

options.path: Capture the official reserve page per club
options.detail: Extend the November capture across the season and join it to the injury table so every 'not listed' cell carries a reserve-list answer.

options.path: Derive it from the transactions log
options.detail: One capture serves two needs (this and S08).
options.risk: A transaction is not proof of current status.

rows.recommended: Capture the official reserve page per club

rows.title: Capture the official transactions log and flag stale depth rows
rows.problem: At least one club still publishes quarterbacks who are on injured reserve. The league's dated transactions pages make staleness computable, but only two of the six ledgers are captured for one month.
rows.buys: Depth rows that carry a truth date, and an alert when they go stale.
rows.risk: The log is high-volume; the flag needs a rule, not a human.

options.path: Daily transactions capture plus a staleness flag per depth row
Weekly capture

rows.recommended: Daily transactions capture plus a staleness flag per depth row

rows.title: Settle the depth-order question before building the deficiency matrix
rows.problem: 149 slots list more than one rank-1 player, two clubs fail to parse, and one publishes its chart as an image.
rows.buys: Either a verified depth order, or a written decision that we derive it from playing time instead.
rows.cost: Three days to verify club by club.
rows.risk: Verification may fail for some clubs, and the brief forbids guessing.

options.path: Verify all 32 club depth pages, one by one, and fall back to snap counts where a club fails
options.risk: The Texans image cannot be parsed by any rule we are allowed to use.

options.path: Derive depth from official snap counts
options.cost: 2 days once snap counts are captured
options.risk: Snap counts describe the past, not the current plan.

rows.recommended: Verify all 32 club depth pages, one by one, and fall back to snap counts where a club fails

rows.title: Start writing the opening price for every market we originate
rows.problem: The price store is closing-only, so the move is invisible and half of closing-line research is out of reach.
rows.buys: Opening-to-closing movement, which is where a lot of origination edge actually shows up.
rows.cost: One day to start; the sample then takes a season.
rows.risk: None technical. The cost is that the sample starts small.

options.path: Snapshot every market at first publication
options.detail: Cheapest possible start; the sample grows from today.

options.path: Buy historical opening prices

rows.recommended: Snapshot every market at first publication

rows.title: Publish a cluster-robust interval next to every ranking
rows.problem: Bets inside the same game are not independent. A per-bet interval is too narrow and makes luck look like skill.
rows.buys: An honest lower bound, which is the whole point of the leaderboard.
rows.risk: Intervals will widen and fewer rules will look significant.

options.path: Cluster by game
options.detail: The natural unit; cheap to compute.

options.path: Cluster by game and week
options.risk: May leave nothing significant, which is information.

rows.recommended: Cluster by game

rows.title: Print a control baseline on every leaderboard run
rows.problem: Without 'favourites only' and 'random' columns, a 6% ROI has nothing to be compared against.
rows.buys: A reader can see whether a strategy beat something a child could have done.
rows.risk: Some strategies will be beaten by the favourite.

options.path: Two control rows on every table
A separate controls page

rows.recommended: Two control rows on every table

rows.title: Prove registration precedes results for every rule on the board
rows.problem: At least one commit carries a strategy's rule and its results together, so the board cannot yet claim to be free of result-chasing.
rows.buys: The one claim that makes the leaderboard worth anything.
rows.risk: Some rules may have to be withdrawn.

options.path: Audit every rule and withdraw any that cannot show a prior commit
options.detail: Costly in reputation, correct in method.

options.path: Re-register the suspect rules going forward and mark the old numbers historical

rows.recommended: Audit every rule and withdraw any that cannot show a prior commit

rows.title: Keep backtest numbers off the leaderboard entirely
rows.problem: Backtest figures are printed on the landing leaderboard today (bets, win %, ROI, ROI interval).
rows.buys: Compliance with the brief and the removal of the strongest temptation on the site.
rows.risk: The leaderboard will look emptier.

options.path: Two boards: a retrospective research table and a prospective board
One board, prospective only

rows.recommended: Two boards: a retrospective research table and a prospective board

rows.title: Rank the combos only behind a validated joint probability
rows.problem: Multiplying marginal probabilities under dependence is wrong, and we store no operator void/push rules.
rows.buys: Three of the four leaderboard divisions stop being empty for a good reason rather than an unexplained one.
rows.cost: Three days to validate a joint model.
rows.risk: The joint model may not beat the marginals enough to matter.

options.path: Validate a joint model on held-out data first
options.detail: The only route the brief permits.

options.path: Leave the divisions empty and say why

rows.recommended: Validate a joint model on held-out data first

rows.title: Transcribe the venue of every fixture from the official game centre
rows.problem: This is the one brief line with nothing behind it; we hold a stadium column from a parsed feed instead.
rows.buys: A closed requirement and the foundation for the roof and weather overlay.
rows.cost: 14 reads to prove the method, then automation.
rows.risk: Game-centre pages may not expose the venue in text.

options.path: Transcribe one week by hand, then automate
options.detail: Proves the page can be read before committing to a scraper.

options.path: Accept the parsed feed's stadium column
options.risk: Not an official transcription; the brief rejects it.

rows.recommended: Transcribe one week by hand, then automate

rows.title: Put a row-count pin on the injury scraper
rows.problem: Two rows went missing in one scrape and nothing failed.
rows.buys: Counts that can be trusted, which every other number depends on.
rows.risk: Builds will fail when the league legitimately changes the page. That is the point.

options.path: Pin the row count and the required fields; fail the build
Pin and warn

rows.recommended: Pin the row count and the required fields; fail the build

rows.title: Decide the public and private split before more raw rows are published
rows.problem: Raw rows are on the live site. The nfl.com terms have now been read verbatim and stored as a clause record; four points in it are not covered by the earlier flag and are waiting on the owner.
rows.buys: A defensible position instead of an accidental one.
rows.risk: Migration may break links that other pages depend on.

options.path: Read the terms, then move raw rows out of the Pages tree
options.detail: What the brief asks, now that the clause record exists to decide against.

options.path: Keep raw rows public and record the decision

rows.recommended: Read the clause record, record the decision, then move raw rows out of the Pages tree if it goes that way

rows.title: Publish the reconciliation as a standing check, not a one-off
rows.problem: This session reconciled 32 of 32 clubs by hand. Nothing stops the next feed refresh from breaking it silently.
rows.buys: A number that is re-proven every time the data moves.
rows.risk: The check will fail whenever the feed is stale, which is why S01 should land first.

options.path: Add the reconciliation to the build and fail on any mismatch
options.risk: Fails while the feed is stale.

options.path: Run it weekly and publish the result
options.risk: A week of bad data can pass unnoticed.

rows.recommended: Add the reconciliation to the build and fail on any mismatch

rows.title: Collapse six overlapping site generations into one navigation
rows.problem: Five or six generations of pages coexist, each with its own nav and its own numbers. A reader cannot tell which one is current.
rows.buys: A site a reader can believe.
rows.cost: Two days plus a decision on what to retire.
rows.risk: Retiring pages can break links other sessions depend on.

options.path: One landing page that links to every generation, with a 'current' badge on one
options.detail: Additive; nothing is deleted; the reader is told which is which.

options.path: Merge the generations
options.risk: Destroys merged work if done carelessly.

rows.recommended: One landing page that links to every generation, with a 'current' badge on one
rows.evidence: This session added console/ alongside the existing generations rather than rewriting them
